description: A hard clipper with an outer limit the signal cannot pass and an inner limit it is either pushed outside of or pulled to silence inside

params.text: Chooses what the inner limit does to a signal inside it: Pull sets that signal to 0V, and Push moves it out to the upper edge when it is positive and to the lower edge when it is negative
Switches the outer limit on and off; with it off the signal leaves at whatever level the gain and the inner limit give it, which can be larger than the signal that came in
Multiplies the signal before either limit is applied, from silence at the counter-clockwise end to twice at the clockwise end
Sets how far the inner limit reaches either side of its centre, 0V at the counter-clockwise end to 10V at the clockwise end
Sets how far the outer limit reaches either side of its centre, 0V at the counter-clockwise end to 10V at the clockwise end, with 5V at the middle of its travel

inputs.text: The signal to be clipped; the number of channels on the cable here sets the number of channels at the output
Adds to the gain knob, 0.1 of a multiplication per volt, so 10V here doubles what the knob gives
Widens the inner limit by 0.5V per volt, added to whatever the push knob gives
Moves the centre of the inner limit away from 0V, one volt of movement per volt
Widens the outer limit by 0.5V per volt, added to whatever the limit knob gives
Moves the centre of the outer limit away from 0V, one volt of movement per volt

outputs.text: The clipped signal, carrying as many channels as the cable at the input

notes: each limit is measured either side of its own centre, so a position input moves the whole window rather than one edge, and a wide offset inner limit can push a signal well away from 0V.
the inner limit is applied first and the outer limit second, so the outer limit catches anything the inner one pushed out.

inputs.1:
0 to 10V · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
